en: Dharma Master Dao’an’s Praise for Recollecting the Buddha Among the thirteen heavens, the Buddha is most honored; Among all things, nothing is more noble than man.
The eye of this world is [the Buddha]; May these wondrous verses exhort you to enter the gate of goodness.
I only fear that sentient beings will commit various evils; The sutras, vinayas, and dharma teachings instruct one to cultivate the body, yet those who eat meat suffer short lifespans.
Relying on the Buddha’s compassion, I urge you, O Ruler, not to speak such words;
Good and evil deeds are always known and heard by the young attendants.
Good deeds and evil deeds... [omitted] ...many people commit evil while cultivating little merit; therefore, sentient beings long suffer in poverty, while no one goes to the blissful heavens;
they vie with one another to rush into the miserable places of hell.
It is not that King Yama’s granary has opened its doors, nor is it that the Buddhas lack compassion;
it is entirely because of the difficulty of exhorting those who are stingy and greedy, who have brought ruin upon themselves through hundreds and thousands of lifetimes.
First, when holding office, do not deceive the Dharma; do not rely on your power and position to act with arrogance and greed.
All wriggling creatures cherish their lives; They carry their bones and bury their bodies, never letting go.
When misfortune or injustice strikes, they suffer deceit and calamity; Beyond the law, they are delayed and punished, yet dare not resent.
To take a single coin by force brings ten-thousandfold retribution; At the end of life, one undergoes hardship in hell.
Wealth and nobility were obtained through rare acts of giving in past lives; poverty is the karmic cause of past stinginess and greed.
The people of this world lack compassion and are fond of wine and meat;
they prepare a hundred flavors to encourage their relatives, yet they fail to realize that the pigs and sheep are being slaughtered. The sounds of their suffering reach the ears of the Supreme Deity.
The gaze of the eyes has long since fallen upon the body; With four legs raised high and low, one approaches the blood-basin.
One should know that those who slaughter others for their flesh Will find no end to their enemies in hell, beyond all reckoning.
For months on end, not a single being is spared; All day long, those who eat meat receive only empty stains.
Death and birth still come; where is there a beautiful place of life? Who does not seek for their life to endure forever?
Transmigrating through the six realms and receiving various forms, They change heads and faces until they do not recognize one another.
They take only the flesh and blood of sentient beings to eat; Who knows them as their own parents, wives, or children?
All pigs and sheep cherish their lives; in their cries of lamentation, sorrow fills their mouths.
Bound by the inferior power of karma, they take the lives of others; through hundreds of kalpas and thousands of births, they shall not cast off their skins.
Both good and evil are reflected in the mirror of karma; driven step by step, they enter Avīci Hell.
I universally exhort all sentient beings to cultivate the myriad practices; now that you have encountered this Dharma teaching, do not give rise to doubt.
With resolute sincerity, listen to the wondrous Dharma, and take the Land of Ultimate Bliss as your future destination.
